title: The rainbow (Genesis 9:8–17)
hookLine: God hangs up his bow in the clouds: never again

lines: A GESTURE YOU CAN STILL SEE.
cards: When two old enemies make peace, there's often a gesture. Swords laid on a table. A flag lowered.

Something you can see that says: this is over. Noah's family has stepped out of the ark onto a scrubbed, silent earth. Everything they knew is gone, and the next time a storm cloud rolls in, they might wonder.
So God speaks, not only to Noah, but past him, to everything that breathes, and makes a gesture you can still see after a summer storm.

teach.b: Covenant, in Hebrew berit, is a binding promise between two parties, the kind of solemn agreement that holds a family, a nation or a marriage together. This one is unusual.
Listen to who it's with: Noah, his sons, their children after them, and every living creature, the birds, the cattle, every beast of the earth. Not just people. Animals too.
And listen to what it asks of them. Nothing. There are no conditions on this side of it.
God simply binds himself: "neither shall there any more be a flood to destroy the earth."
Then the sign, in the King James Bible: "I do set my bow in the cloud, and it shall be for a token of a covenant between me and the earth."

The Hebrew word for rainbow, qeshet, is the ordinary word for a bow, the weapon, the kind a warrior draws. Some readers picture it this way: God hanging the war bow up in the sky, unstrung, pointed away from the earth.
Then a question: who is the sign for? You'd think it's for people, to calm them down when the clouds come. But God says, I will look upon it, that I may remember the everlasting covenant.

teach.h: A REMINDER GOD SETS FOR HIMSELF.
teach.b: The rainbow is a token for the earth, and a reminder God sets for himself.

teach.h: I DO SET MY BOW IN THE CLOUD.
teach.b: The same word as the flood's turning point: God remembers. Christians have gone on to speak of other covenants in the Bible, with Abraham, at Sinai, and the new covenant at the Last Supper.
They start here, with every living thing, and a bow hung in the clouds.

how: Covenant runs through Christian teaching, from the promise to Noah to the new covenant Jesus names at the Last Supper, and churches recall the new covenant at communion, in Jesus' words over the cup.

games.q: the flood is over. God makes a covenant with every living thing. what does God ask them to do in return?
games.why: there are no conditions on their side. "neither shall there any more be a flood to destroy the earth."

practice: If you're near a window, look out at the sky; if not, picture the last sky you saw, and let your eyes rest on whatever color is in it. Then think of a promise someone keeps to you without asking anything back.
If you pray, you can give thanks for promises kept.
